title: Apple GPU prefill 2x2 register ownership versus scalar direct control
question: With the same BM=8, BN=16 output tile and direct full-K streaming, does assigning each lane a 2x2 output microtile improve rotating packed-QKV prefill over assigning each thread one scalar output?
hypothesis: For a complete output tile, 2x2 ownership halves source-requested X and W operand loads by reusing two X values across two columns and two W values across two rows. That reuse may repay four live FP32 accumulators per lane and the reduction from a 128-thread group to one 32-lane SIMD group.

control.ownership: One 128-thread group owns one 8x16 output rectangle; one thread owns one scalar output and one persistent FP32 accumulator.
control.k_mapping: Each valid thread walks all K=896 values serially and loads X and W directly from device memory.

candidate.ownership: One 32-thread SIMD group owns the same 8x16 output rectangle; each lane owns a 2x2 microtile and four persistent FP32 accumulators.
candidate.k_mapping: Each valid lane walks all K=896 values serially, loading up to two X values and two W values per K step and forming four products.

changed_mechanism: The candidate changes arithmetic ownership, threadgroup width, live accumulator count, source-requested operand loads, and generated code. It does not introduce shared operand staging, K blocking, barriers, or Apple matrix operations.
unchanged: BF16 input, weight, bias, and output with FP32 accumulation and one final BF16 cast
row-major X[M,K], W[N,K], and Y[M,N] layouts
full-K direct streaming with no BK phases
zero threadgroup operand scratch and zero threadgroup barriers
one enqueue per layer and one completion boundary per measured workload
K=896, N=1152, and 24 distinct rotating weight allocations
no weight packing, quantization, Apple matrix primitive, or public dispatch change

correctness.authority: tests/test_linear.mojo plus each timed specialization's untimed exact-unit-output gate
required_cases: Existing scalar direct-control oracle, exact-tile, ragged-tail, and Qwen-width cases
2x2 candidate exact M=8 K=32 N=16 tile
2x2 candidate ragged M=9 K=129 N=17 tails
Exact BF16 unit output at K=896 and N=1152 before timing every benchmark specialization
Existing rowwise, shared-staging, decode, and packed-QKV tests remain passing

workload_matrix.weights: 24 distinct allocations rotated once per measured workload iteration

measurement_protocol.paired_statistic: Within each block and M, 2x2-register median divided by direct median; summarize the four ratios with their median and retain every ratio.
measurement_protocol.environment: Clean immutable commit, AC power, no reported thermal or performance warning, Apple GPU plus Metal runtime identity, and MODULAR_DEBUG unset.

classification_rule.material_improvement: Median paired ratio <= 0.95 and 2x2-register faster in at least three of four blocks.
classification_rule.material_regression: Median paired ratio >= 1.05 and 2x2-register slower in at least three of four blocks.

decision_rule.advance: Advance the 2x2 register candidate to a final public-rowwise comparison only if it materially improves M=64, 128, and 256 and does not materially regress any tested M>=8.
decision_rule.reject: If the candidate materially regresses M=64, 128, and 256, stop manual register-tile shape search and move to a hardware-matrix experiment.
decision_rule.otherwise: Make no advance or production change; retain the result as mixed or inconclusive before designing another experiment.
decision_rule.production_decision: None. Even an advancing result cannot select a public dispatch path.

nonclaims: The comparison isolates the complete arithmetic-ownership change, not an individual occupancy, register, cache, instruction, scheduling, or compiler effect.
Requested traffic is source-derived and is not observed hardware cache, fabric, or DRAM traffic.
A win against direct would not establish a win against the public SIMD-group rowwise kernel.
A loss would reject this 2x2 shape for this workload, not all manual register tiling or hardware-matrix mappings.
No Apple matrix primitive, Neural Engine, tensor-core analog, end-to-end prompt, model, or decoder throughput result.

decision.finding: The 2x2 register mapping materially improved M=16 through M=256, including 60.65%, 62.06%, and 62.19% improvements at the decisive M=64, 128, and 256 rows, and was faster in all four blocks at every M>=8.
decision.small_m_boundary: M=1 materially regressed by 122.73%, M=4 was inconclusive at +1.12%, and M=8 was inconclusive at -3.66% despite being faster in four of four blocks.
decision.scope: Advance only to a paired public-rowwise comparison; the result does not select a public dispatch path and does not evaluate an Apple matrix primitive.
decision.next_experiment: Compare the 2x2 register mapping directly with enqueue_linear_apple_gpu across the same prefill row range before deciding whether to pursue public dispatch or Apple matrix operations.
